Aristocratic Buenos Aires!
Join us on a walk through two of the most architecturally impressive neighborhoods of Buenos Aires, home to the French-obsessed oligarchic elites of late 1800, who tried to shape Buenos Aires after the French capital.

Discover the glamour and extravagance of the "Paris of South America" by visiting Retiro and Recoleta. The chosen neighbourhoods by Argentina's French-obsessed economic (and oligarchic) elites in the late 1800s and the beginning of the 20th century, where they constructed 60-room French palaces to show off their wealth and power, and competed for fame and influence.

The golden age of Argentina, stories of love and revenge that echo through time, quirks, and bizarre facts and habits of Buenos Aires and its people, "los porteños".
Go back into the glamour of the old days, as you learn about Argentina's "Belle Époque", and how their fortunes (and misfortunes) intertwined with the ups and downs of the country throughout the 20th century and all the way until today.

During the tour, we will see: 

  • San Martín Square: 
  1.  - Anchorena Palace 
  2.  - Kavanagh building
  3.  - Paz Palace
  4.  - Monument to José de San Martín (Argentina's main National Hero)
  • The Monumental Tower (formerly known as the British Tower)
  • Arroyo Street
  • Embassy of France
  • Embassy of Brazil
  • Alvear Avenue: home to Argentina's finest palaces


Useful information:

  1. The tour will end at the Plaza Francia, right in front of the Cemetery of Recoleta. 
  2. This tour DOES NOT include the cemetery

Do you want to discover the nature of Buenos Aires?


Come and visit the Costanera Sur Ecological Reserve!


With an area of about 350 hectares, this is the largest green space in the City of Buenos Aires. Here, various natural environments representative of the Rio de la Plata Coast are preserved: wetlands, marginal jungle, thorn forest, and grassland will be the settings where we can appreciate a great amount of biological diversity.

Its more than 500 species of plants, butterflies, reptiles, amphibians, and small mammals will accompany us during the tour. Additionally, we will be able to observe and listen to some of the more than 300 species of birds that visit the reserve. This is why this site has been declared a wetland of international importance, as well as an important area for bird conservation.  


You will be able to take incredible photos of Buenos Aires nature and the majestic Río de la Plata, the widest estuary in the world!


This tour is ideal for nature and outdoor enthusiasts.

Are you ready to explore this place with us?

Cradle of Tango and Porteño Culture Buenos Aires Free Tour","slug":"69004-abasto-cradle-of-tango-and-porteno-culture-buenos-aires-free-tour","description_html":"

Discover El Abasto, the "unofficial" neighborhood of Buenos Aires. The quintessential "arrabalero," home to the undisputed Carlos Gardel. You will uncover the fascinating history behind one of the most emblematic buildings: the Mercado de Abasto. Be amazed by all the details of the emergence of a unique and unrepeatable neighborhood.

We will travel back to the beginning, to the golden times: the boom and expansion of the area; also to its closure and abandonment, until its resurgence and the current context. For over a century, El Abasto welcomed immigrants and locals, creating its own identity. Theaters, circuses, inns, canteens, and bars were established, giving it a unique, picturesque lifestyle, full of great stories and anecdotes that we will discover in its streets to understand the keys to the porteño spirit.

We will visit the places where Gardel began, his house, bars, and the secrets of an epic life. You will also get to know the authentic world of tango venues, milongas, and tango houses like a local, not in an artificial way.

Don't miss the opportunity to experience the secrets of a mythical neighborhood where the identity of Buenos Aires was forged.

To explore at your leisure: nestled among elegant streets and historic buildings, lies a hidden gem that few know about. Time seems to stand still, the atmosphere beckons you to linger, and every detail holds a story. Secrets few travelers are aware of. Shall we explore a small part of the Recoleta and Palermo neighborhoods?

We'll visit the Floralis Genérica, Public Television, the Evita Monument and the National Library, and the Automobile Museum. What stories do they hold? We'll explore Palermo Chico: What role did its grand houses play in the early 20th century? We'll also visit the Errázuriz Palace and the National San Martín Institute. Don't miss this journey through our history!

","slug":"69009-the-iconic-landmarks-of-downtown-buenos-aires","description_html":"

Welcome to the San Nicolás and Retiro neighborhoods. I designed this tour to show you the city's most iconic landmarks. I am a certified guide, accredited by the Buenos Aires City Tourism Board and the Buenos Aires City Guides Association. I combine professionalism and the rigor that comes from my years of experience (as a teacher, cultural manager, and tour guide). If you want to explore the city and enjoy history, art, photography, and architecture, take this tour to visit and photograph its landmarks.

  • The first section is known as the "Microcentro," around the Church of San Nicolás de Bari, where the obelisk stands today. The second, the Retiro neighborhood, was a residential area with country estates away from the city center, taking its name from the governor's residence. Today, it is one of the most French-influenced areas, along with Recoleta.
Meeting point : Vatican Square, in the block bounded by Cerrito, Viamonte, Libertad, and Pasaje Toscanini streets. We will meet at the corner of Cerrito and Viamonte, next to the Colón Theatre.
Recommendation: Book your guided tour of the Teatro Colón one hour before your Guruwalk walking tour.

  • Colón Theatre
  • Lavalle Square - Palace of Justice
  • Obelisk
  • Avenida Diagonal Norte- Avenida Presidente Roque Saenz Peña and its corner of five domes.
  • Florida Street
  • Guemes Gallery
  • Galerías Pacífico (optional: admission to the Borges Cultural Center/Museum of Oriental Art)
  • Naval Center

On this tour, you'll discover Monserrat, the oldest neighborhood in Buenos Aires, which grew alongside the origins of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. Here, Argentina was forged and became its historical cradle. You'll visit its churches, its oldest pharmacy and bookstore, its first university, and, among other sites, a Jugendstil (German Modernist) building, a variant of Art Nouveau, blended with eclecticism and Neo-Gothic touches. And I'll tell you the stories of the pioneers who transformed a village of dirt roads into one of the most European-looking cities in South America.

I am a certified tour guide, registered with the Buenos Aires City Tourism Board and the Buenos Aires City Tour Guides Association (AGuitBa), and I specialize in cultural tourism. My goal is to transport you along a timeline from colonial Buenos Aires to contemporary Buenos Aires. And Buenos Aires offers a wonderful array of possibilities; whether strolling through its streets, admiring its monuments, visiting its museums, or savoring its culinary specialties.
What are they going to see?

  • Montserrat

 Plaza de Mayo.

 La Estrella Pharmacy (with entrance)

 Santo Domingo Convent - Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary (with entrance)

 Otto Wulff Building (external view)

 Monument to Roca

 Buenos Aires City Legislature (external view)

 London City Confectionery (entrance fee applies, but consumption is optional)

  • I'm Inés Cordonnier, and I've walked these cobblestones many times, not as a tourist, but as someone seeking to understand the city I love. And I want to share the richness and diversity of Buenos Aires with each of you. This tour isn't a job; it's a conversation that is renewed and enriched every time I do it . My mobile number is +54 9 11 36711315.
  • Meeting point: Pyramid of May, in the center of Plaza de Mayo, in the Monserrat neighborhood. It is located specifically in front of the Casa Rosada and the Metropolitan Cathedral, between Hipólito Yrigoyen, Bolívar, Avenida Rivadavia and Balcarce streets.

Can you imagine touring Buenos Aires and discovering that behind its most iconic buildings lie stories of conspiracies, betrayals, and murders?

In this guided tour, I invite you to dive into the heart of downtown Buenos Aires to uncover the hidden side of Argentine history. Every facade we will observe is not random: its shape, style, and location reveal the political, economic, and cultural context in which they were built. Nothing is left to chance. 


As we walk, we will unravel the secret plots that defined the course of the country: hidden plans, unexpected alliances, and power struggles woven in the shadows. From the British invasions, when Buenos Aires was just a colonial stronghold, to the tumultuous 1950s, this tour shows you how the city was the stage for intrigues so incredible they seem straight out of a novel.

It's not just a walk: it's an experience to see the city with new eyes, understand why it is the way it is, and discover that at every corner, a game was played that changed history.

The Recoleta Cemetery is an open-air museum. There are many guides, but my experience guarantees that you will learn about our customs, ideas, feelings, and also history!
I will tell you the story of Argentina's most influential figures, the aristocratic families that created the Paris in Buenos Aires, the most interesting legends, mysterious tales, stories of love and power. Nobel laureates, politicians, women who made history. And if we add that I take the best photos so you can take the best memory of Baires...
Oh, I almost forgot, if you like to read, I can offer you recommended readings, movies, books, etc.
Are you going to miss it? I'm waiting for you!

results.name: Free tour Retiro and Recoleta: Aristocratic Buenos Aires
results.description_html:
Aristocratic Buenos Aires!
Join us on a walk through two of the most architecturally impressive neighborhoods of Buenos Aires, home to the French-obsessed oligarchic elites of late 1800, who tried to shape Buenos Aires after the French capital.

Discover the glamour and extravagance of the "Paris of South America" by visiting Retiro and Recoleta. The chosen neighbourhoods by Argentina's French-obsessed economic (and oligarchic) elites in the late 1800s and the beginning of the 20th century, where they constructed 60-room French palaces to show off their wealth and power, and competed for fame and influence.

The golden age of Argentina, stories of love and revenge that echo through time, quirks, and bizarre facts and habits of Buenos Aires and its people, "los porteños".
Go back into the glamour of the old days, as you learn about Argentina's "Belle Époque", and how their fortunes (and misfortunes) intertwined with the ups and downs of the country throughout the 20th century and all the way until today.

During the tour, we will see: 

  • San Martín Square: 
  1.  - Anchorena Palace 
  2.  - Kavanagh building
  3.  - Paz Palace
  4.  - Monument to José de San Martín (Argentina's main National Hero)
  • The Monumental Tower (formerly known as the British Tower)
  • Arroyo Street
  • Embassy of France
  • Embassy of Brazil
  • Alvear Avenue: home to Argentina's finest palaces


Useful information:

  1. The tour will end at the Plaza Francia, right in front of the Cemetery of Recoleta. 
  2. This tour DOES NOT include the cemetery

results.name: A Natural Oasis in Buenos Aires: Discover Costanera Sur!
results.description_html:
Do you want to discover the nature of Buenos Aires?


Come and visit the Costanera Sur Ecological Reserve!


With an area of about 350 hectares, this is the largest green space in the City of Buenos Aires. Here, various natural environments representative of the Rio de la Plata Coast are preserved: wetlands, marginal jungle, thorn forest, and grassland will be the settings where we can appreciate a great amount of biological diversity.

Its more than 500 species of plants, butterflies, reptiles, amphibians, and small mammals will accompany us during the tour. Additionally, we will be able to observe and listen to some of the more than 300 species of birds that visit the reserve. This is why this site has been declared a wetland of international importance, as well as an important area for bird conservation.  


You will be able to take incredible photos of Buenos Aires nature and the majestic Río de la Plata, the widest estuary in the world!


This tour is ideal for nature and outdoor enthusiasts.

Are you ready to explore this place with us?

results.name: Abasto, Cradle of Tango and Porteño Culture Buenos Aires Free Tour
results.description_html:
Discover El Abasto, the "unofficial" neighborhood of Buenos Aires. The quintessential "arrabalero," home to the undisputed Carlos Gardel. You will uncover the fascinating history behind one of the most emblematic buildings: the Mercado de Abasto. Be amazed by all the details of the emergence of a unique and unrepeatable neighborhood.

We will travel back to the beginning, to the golden times: the boom and expansion of the area; also to its closure and abandonment, until its resurgence and the current context. For over a century, El Abasto welcomed immigrants and locals, creating its own identity. Theaters, circuses, inns, canteens, and bars were established, giving it a unique, picturesque lifestyle, full of great stories and anecdotes that we will discover in its streets to understand the keys to the porteño spirit.

We will visit the places where Gardel began, his house, bars, and the secrets of an epic life. You will also get to know the authentic world of tango venues, milongas, and tango houses like a local, not in an artificial way.

Don't miss the opportunity to experience the secrets of a mythical neighborhood where the identity of Buenos Aires was forged.

results.name: A corner of Recoleta and Palermo Chico
results.description_html:
To explore at your leisure: nestled among elegant streets and historic buildings, lies a hidden gem that few know about. Time seems to stand still, the atmosphere beckons you to linger, and every detail holds a story. Secrets few travelers are aware of. Shall we explore a small part of the Recoleta and Palermo neighborhoods?

We'll visit the Floralis Genérica, Public Television, the Evita Monument and the National Library, and the Automobile Museum. What stories do they hold? We'll explore Palermo Chico: What role did its grand houses play in the early 20th century? We'll also visit the Errázuriz Palace and the National San Martín Institute. Don't miss this journey through our history!

results.name: The iconic landmarks of downtown Buenos Aires.
results.description_html:
Welcome to the San Nicolás and Retiro neighborhoods. I designed this tour to show you the city's most iconic landmarks. I am a certified guide, accredited by the Buenos Aires City Tourism Board and the Buenos Aires City Guides Association. I combine professionalism and the rigor that comes from my years of experience (as a teacher, cultural manager, and tour guide). If you want to explore the city and enjoy history, art, photography, and architecture, take this tour to visit and photograph its landmarks.

  • The first section is known as the "Microcentro," around the Church of San Nicolás de Bari, where the obelisk stands today. The second, the Retiro neighborhood, was a residential area with country estates away from the city center, taking its name from the governor's residence. Today, it is one of the most French-influenced areas, along with Recoleta.
Meeting point : Vatican Square, in the block bounded by Cerrito, Viamonte, Libertad, and Pasaje Toscanini streets. We will meet at the corner of Cerrito and Viamonte, next to the Colón Theatre.
Recommendation: Book your guided tour of the Teatro Colón one hour before your Guruwalk walking tour.

results.name: Montserrat, cradle of the viceroyalty.
results.description_html:
On this tour, you'll discover Monserrat, the oldest neighborhood in Buenos Aires, which grew alongside the origins of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. Here, Argentina was forged and became its historical cradle. You'll visit its churches, its oldest pharmacy and bookstore, its first university, and, among other sites, a Jugendstil (German Modernist) building, a variant of Art Nouveau, blended with eclecticism and Neo-Gothic touches. And I'll tell you the stories of the pioneers who transformed a village of dirt roads into one of the most European-looking cities in South America.

I am a certified tour guide, registered with the Buenos Aires City Tourism Board and the Buenos Aires City Tour Guides Association (AGuitBa), and I specialize in cultural tourism. My goal is to transport you along a timeline from colonial Buenos Aires to contemporary Buenos Aires. And Buenos Aires offers a wonderful array of possibilities; whether strolling through its streets, admiring its monuments, visiting its museums, or savoring its culinary specialties.
What are they going to see?

  • Montserrat

 Defensa Street

 Basilica and Convent of Saint Francis of Assisi (with entrance)

  • I'm Inés Cordonnier, and I've walked these cobblestones many times, not as a tourist, but as someone seeking to understand the city I love. And I want to share the richness and diversity of Buenos Aires with each of you. This tour isn't a job; it's a conversation that is renewed and enriched every time I do it . My mobile number is +54 9 11 36711315.

results.name: Free Tour of Conspiracies in Argentine History
results.description_html:
Can you imagine touring Buenos Aires and discovering that behind its most iconic buildings lie stories of conspiracies, betrayals, and murders?

In this guided tour, I invite you to dive into the heart of downtown Buenos Aires to uncover the hidden side of Argentine history. Every facade we will observe is not random: its shape, style, and location reveal the political, economic, and cultural context in which they were built. Nothing is left to chance. 


As we walk, we will unravel the secret plots that defined the course of the country: hidden plans, unexpected alliances, and power struggles woven in the shadows. From the British invasions, when Buenos Aires was just a colonial stronghold, to the tumultuous 1950s, this tour shows you how the city was the stage for intrigues so incredible they seem straight out of a novel.

It's not just a walk: it's an experience to see the city with new eyes, understand why it is the way it is, and discover that at every corner, a game was played that changed history.
